page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features an arm64 architecture utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 (ARMv8) CPU model. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1532.99, and the multi-core score is 6110.35. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 386.53 GB/sec and a large block uncached speed of 107.62 GB/sec, while large block write speed reaches 39.3 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at 24.04 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 9.41 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weaker at 29.46 GB/sec. Geekbench scores include 1502.0 for single-core and 4871.0 for multi-core, with average performance in software compilation (6328.0) and image processing (4365.0), but weaker results in ray tracing (4689.0).

The instance exhibits specific performance tradeoffs, particularly in cryptographic and complex instruction sets. The Passmark CPU encryption test yields a poor score of 554.37, and the extended instructions test is weak at 3310.41. Large language model inference is also limited, with text generation for a 7B model scoring a poor 5.4 tokens/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gd.xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-storage profile, combining dedicated ARM cores with high-speed local NVMe storage without the overhead of external network-attached storage. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight containerized applications that benefit from local scratch space and dedicated CPU allocation.
description: The Amazon Web Services c7gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 AWS Neoverse-V1 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz, it includes 8.0 GB of memory and a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers average performance in standard CPU benchmarks, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4871.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 6110.35. It exhibits high memory read bandwidth, reaching 386.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks. However, it shows performance limitations in cryptographic operations and large language model inference. Qualitatively, the instance provides a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring dedicated ARM resources and fast local storage. It is well-suited for static web serving, software compilation, database tasks, and general compute workloads that utilize local scratch space.
